did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with a promise that the LORD will restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem—that is, return his people and their national status to their rightful place.
Did you know? The nations are gathered in the Valley of Jehoshaphat so that the LORD may judge them for scattering Israel, dividing the land, and harming his inheritance.
Did you know? The verse describes the humiliation of the people of Judah at the hands of the nations, including casting lots for captives and selling children in exchange for a drink.
Did you know? Among the accusations against Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia is that they took silver, gold, and precious treasures and carried them into the temples of their gods.
Did you know? The chapter says that the people of Judah and Jerusalem were sold to the Greeks to remove them far from their land—a description of trading captives and exiling them.
Did you know? The nations are called to proclaim war and gather together as part of their preparation for divine judgment in the Valley of Jehoshaphat.
Did you know? In the description of the war, farm tools are turned into weapons: plowshares become swords and pruning hooks become spears; even the weak are told to say, “I am a warrior.”
Did you know? Judgment is portrayed through images of harvest and wine-making: the harvest is ripe, the winepress is full, and the vats overflow because the nations are so wicked.
Did you know? On the day of the LORD, the sun and moon grow dark and the stars withdraw their light—a description of cosmic upheaval accompanying the day of judgment.

Did you know? Alongside the descriptions of judgment and destruction, the chapter ends with a picture of abundance in Judah: sweet wine flowing from the mountains, milk from the hills, water in the streambeds, and a spring flowing from the house of the LORD.
